# The Temple of the Hearth

## Description
A round stone hall on Temple Lane with a fire pit at its center that has, by rule,
never gone out. Benches ring the fire; the smoke goes up through a copper hood. Mother
Temperance Quill keeps the place, dispenses soup, blessings and unasked-for advice, and
has strong views about Midwinter ("a pagan racket, but the soup sells"). The temple
takes in anyone snowed-in, which this year is everyone.

## Areas
- **hall** — the door from Temple Lane; the fire; benches; soup
- **vestry** — behind a curtain north of the fire; Mother Temperance's books and cot
- **crypt** — stair under the vestry (z −10); the old shrines, including a small one to "the First Winter King" nobody tends

## Items & features
- The fire: never out; a toast made over it ends normally, which Mother Temperance will point out
- Soup: free; good; restores 1 HP and a sense of proportion
- The Hymnal of the Hearth (vestry): has the Midwinter song in it, all nine verses, including the one about the Crown ("five stones to the crown and one to the king / a toast and a dance and a song and a sting / and Prudence to tell him when not to do a thing")
- The First Winter King's shrine (crypt): a stone goose. Nobody knows why

## Hidden
- DC 13 (hall): the same three townsfolk come in for soup, say the same three things, and leave by the same door, in the same order, every hour
- DC 16 (crypt): the stone goose's eyes are two chips of the same dull grey as the Crown's one remaining setting

(none authored; the temple is sanctuary)
